subdomain: 1.4 Design multi-agent systems and orchestration strategies

en.question: A lead agent delegates supplier investigations, but workers repeatedly inspect the same suppliers and omit required evidence. The tools function correctly. Which delegation change most directly addresses the coordination problem?

options.text: Give each worker the full research request and encourage it to pursue the sources it finds most promising.
options.note: A shared broad request leaves ownership ambiguous. Independent workers can choose the same attractive sources while all neglecting less obvious requirements.

options.text: Define each worker's objective, supplier scope, source guidance, output format, evidence requirements, and boundaries with other assignments.
options.note: An explicit delegation contract establishes both what to cover and what belongs elsewhere. This directly addresses duplicated work and missing evidence.

options.text: Increase each worker's token budget and preserve its original task description to avoid disrupting its search strategy.
options.note: More search effort does not clarify which suppliers or evidence each worker owns. It can amplify overlapping work under the same ambiguous assignment.

options.text: Ask the synthesis agent to remove duplicate paragraphs after workers finish, without changing their assignments or source guidance.
options.note: Post-processing can remove repeated prose but cannot recover evidence nobody collected. The coordination defect starts at delegation, not final wording.

references.title: How we built our multi-agent research system
